<thought>Based on the 13C NMR data, the aliphatic carbon signals are at 52.24 ppm, 49.55 ppm, 43.55 ppm, and 19.23 ppm. The peak at 19.23 ppm falls in the typical range for a methyl carbon (CH₃ attached to another carbon). The signal at ~52 ppm is characteristic of a methoxy (O‑CH₃) group, which is also a methyl. The remaining two aliphatic signals (≈44–50 ppm) are more consistent with methylene or carbon attached to heteroatoms rather than methyls. Therefore, the molecule contains **2 methyl (CH₃) groups**.</thought>
<final_answer>2</final_answer>
